A golden hat trick is an unofficial term for scoring four goals in a single match. It is not an official rule and is used only in some sports discussions. What Is the Greatest Hat Trick of All Time? Many consider Geoff Hurst’s hat trick in the 1966 FIFA World Cup final the greatest because it remains the only men’s World Cup final hat trick. Who Is the Youngest Player to Get a Hat Trick? Pelé is the youngest player to score a hat trick in a FIFA World Cup. He was 17 years and 244 days old when he achieved it in the 1958 semifinal. What’s the Fastest Hat Trick Ever? The fastest recorded soccer hat trick was scored by Alex Torr in 70 seconds during an English Sunday league match in 2013.

passages.text: If you’ve watched a soccer, hockey, or cricket game, you’ve probably heard the term “hat trick.” It usually means one player has achieved something special by reaching the number three during a single game. Even though the phrase is widely used, its exact meaning depends on the sport. So, what is a hat trick? In soccer and hockey, it means scoring three goals in one match. In cricket, it means taking three wickets with three consecutive balls. Other sports have their own versions too. In this blog, I’ll explain what a hat trick means, how it differs across sports, where the term came from, and why it remains one of the most celebrated individual achievements in sports. What Is a Hat Trick? A hat trick is when a player scores three goals in a single game or match. It is one of the most celebrated individual achievements in many sports, especially soccer, hockey, and cricket (where the term has a different meaning). In soccer and hockey, a hat trick simply means one player scores three goals during the same match, regardless of when the goals are scored. These are both examples of jargon - the specialised vocabulary, technical terms or slang used by a profession, trade or group. You might have heard this term in relation to law or medicine, but football has its own jargon. Well, wonder no more. BBC Bitesize is here to help you learn the origins of some of the best-known and most widely used football terminology - just in time for the 2026 FIFA Men's World Cup! Hat-trick A player gets a hat-trick when they score three goals in one game, but the use of the term actually didnât start on the football pitch. A driver earns a hat trick by taking pole position, recording the fastest lap, and winning the race during the same event. Achieving all three requires qualifying speed, consistent performance during the race, and a reliable car from start to finish. Since many factors can affect the outcome of a race, including weather, tire strategy, and mechanical issues, completing a motorsport hat trick remains an outstanding achievement. How Does a Hat Trick Work in Different Sports? The meaning of a hat trick changes from one sport to another, but the idea behind it stays the same. It recognizes a player or athlete who achieves three standout feats in a single game or event. 1. Soccer In soccer, a hat trick means a player scores three goals in one match. The goals can be scored at any point during the game and do not need to be consecutive. They may come from open play, penalties, or free kicks, as long as all three are officially credited to the same player. passages.text: Hat-trick A hat-trick or hat trick is the achievement of a generally positive feat three times in a match, or another achievement based on the number three.[1] Origin [edit] The term was first used in 1858 in cricket, to describe H. H. Stephenson taking three wickets with three consecutive deliveries. Fans held a collection for Stephenson, and presented him with a hat bought with the proceeds.[2][3][4] The term appeared in print for the first known time in 1865 in the Chelmsford Chronicle.[5] "Hat trick" was eventually adopted by many other sports, including hockey, association football,[6] Formula 1 racing, rugby, water polo, and competitive video games such as Counter-Strike. Use [edit] Bat and ball games [edit] Baseball [edit] In the past, the term was occasionally used to describe when a player struck out three times in a baseball game, and the term golden sombrero was used when a player struck out four times in a game. In recent years, hat trick has been more often used to describe when a player hits three home runs in a game.
